description: Congee with Century Egg is a quintessential Chinese breakfast, offering a comforting and savory start to the day. This creamy rice porridge, slow-cooked to perfection, is studded with the unique, umami-rich flavor of century egg and often enhanced with shredded ginger. It is a beloved dish that nourishes and satisfies with its delicate texture and profound flavors.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice
instructions.text: Wash the jasmine rice thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. For an extra creamy congee, soak the washed rice in 2 cups of water for at least 30 minutes, or even freeze it overnight after soaking.

instructions.title: Start the Congee Base
instructions.text: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, combine the washed rice and 8 cups of fresh water. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over high heat, stirring occasionally to prevent the rice from sticking to the bottom.

instructions.title: Simmer the Porridge
instructions.text: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer gently for 30-40 minutes. Stir every 10-15 minutes to ensure even cooking and prevent sticking. The rice grains should break down and the congee should thicken to a creamy consistency. If it becomes too thick, add more hot water, 1/2 cup at a time.

instructions.title: Prepare Century Eggs and Ginger
instructions.text: While the congee simmers, peel the century eggs and dice them into small, bite-sized pieces. Peel and thinly slice or julienne the fresh ginger.

instructions.title: Add Century Eggs and Season
instructions.text: Once the congee has reached your desired consistency, stir in the diced century eggs and most of the sliced ginger (reserve some for garnish). Add salt and white pepper to taste. If using, stir in the shredded cooked pork or chicken at this stage.

instructions.title: Final Touches and Serve
instructions.text: Let the congee simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Ladle the hot congee into individual bowls. Drizzle with a little sesame oil, garnish with the remaining fresh ginger and sliced green onions. Serve immediately and enjoy this comforting Chinese breakfast.

tips: For extra creamy congee, freeze the washed rice overnight before cooking. The ice crystals help break down the rice grains faster, resulting in a smoother texture.
Always add century egg towards the end of cooking to preserve its unique texture and prevent it from completely dissolving into the porridge.
Serve hot with a drizzle of good quality sesame oil and a sprinkle of white pepper for an authentic taste. A dash of soy sauce can also be added for extra savory depth.
